summary: Scanned sast-demo (3 Python files) with semgrep 1.183.0 and the bundled lab rules, metrics off. 4 raw hits: request data reaches shell=True in /ping (command injection), app.run(debug=True), and a fixed /tmp path opened for writing. The second shell hit in /diag is dismissed: the host is allow-listed by a regex before the sink. semgrep skipped tests/test_ping.py (default ignores); it holds the same pattern but is test code.

findings.title: Request data reaches a shell command in /ping
findings.description: flask.request.args.get("host") flows into subprocess.run("ping -c1 " + host, shell=True) at app.py:10-11 with no validation. Any HTTP client can append shell syntax (?host=;id) and run commands on the server.
findings.remediation: Pass an argument list without a shell: subprocess.run(["ping", "-c1", host], capture_output=True); validate host against an allow-list or socket.inet_aton.

findings.title: Flask app runs with debug=True
findings.description: app.run(debug=True) at app.py:30 enables the Werkzeug debugger. If the app is reachable beyond localhost, the interactive console and leaked source/config follow; the console PIN is the only barrier.

proof.poc: jq '.results[] | select(.check_id | endswith("lab-flask-debug-true")) | {path, start}' evidence/artifacts/semgrep.json && sed -n '29,30p' /home/agent/target/app.py

findings.remediation: Read the flag from the environment: app.run(debug=os.environ.get("FLASK_DEBUG") == "1") and keep it off outside local development.

findings.title: Fixed temp path opened for writing in tools.py
findings.description: store_report() opens /tmp/report.txt for writing at tools.py:6. Another local user can pre-create the path (symlink or file) so the write lands elsewhere.
findings.remediation: Use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile or tempfile.mkstemp for a unique, safely-created file.

hypotheses.title: shell=True on request data in /diag (app.py:20)
hypotheses.rationale: Same sink as SAST-001, but host is validated by re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9.-]{1,64}", host) at app.py:18-19 before the sink: shell metacharacters cannot pass. Dismissed as sanitised.
hypotheses.next_step: None. If the allow-list loosens, re-triage.

hypotheses.title: shell=True on request data in tests/test_ping.py
hypotheses.rationale: semgrep skipped the file under its default ignores (tests/). The file holds the same vulnerable pattern but is test code that is not deployed.
hypotheses.next_step: Confirm tests/ is not shipped in the deployment artefact.

artifacts.description: Raw semgrep report (trimmed to the fields used in triage)
